rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 12 mm apart across x = -0.024 to +0.024 m (the tape is 25 mm wide, so the outer sensors can see the edge), placed 0.03 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the line. A 12 mm footprint keeps the readings smooth. Wheel track 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m, and mass 0.8 kg give a stable, moderately responsive body. Controller: antisymmetric weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] make the signal proportional to lateral error with the correct sign (positive x steers left). base_speed 1.7 is high enough to cover the course in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s average needed) while leaving margin for bends. kp 3.0 gives a firm correction without saturating the wheels on normal errors. ki 0.1 is small, to avoid integral windup on long bends. kd 0.05 damps the oscillation that kp alone would cause. line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot search toward the side it was last on. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with a moderate rms_error and few line-loss events. Expected weak points: overshoot in the slalom and possible speed loss in tight bends. The next race should show whether speed or steering is the limit.
